newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Treu meets industry, metal unions.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Treu meets industry, metal unions.

text.p: Italian Labour Minister Tiziano Treu met engineering and metalworkers unions and employers separately on Thursday in an effort to jump-start stalled talks in a bitter wages dispute.
More talks, still on a separate basis, were set for next Tuesday as industrialists and unions said their positions remained far apart although they saw room to negotiate.
Despite more talks being scheduled, Italian state television reported that unions still intended to go ahead with a strike planned for December 13.
"Negotiations have begun," Treu told reporters after the meetings. "In the name of the government, I have invited the parties to get round the table as soon as possible."
Treu said the invitation to talk had been accepted by both sides, adding: "It seems to me that there is the willingness to proceed swiftly to a consideration of all the questions."

The three trades unions, FIOM, FIM and UILM which represent 1.5 million engineering and metalworkers, are protesting against a refusal by management to compensate workers fully for higher than expected inflation under the past wage contract period.

The dispute stems from differing interpretations of a 1993 labour pact which scrapped the automatic index-linking of salaries on condition that management would make up a shortfall in wages if inflation ran above target.
Unions say the accord means all the inflation overshoot should be covered, but employers argue only a part of lost earnings need be made up.
Since their contracts expired in June, unions have held two eight-hour strikes in September and November and last month called 10 more hours of protests to press home their demands.
In cash terms, unions have asked for a 262,000 lire ($171) rise in their monthly pay packets, with 97,000 of that to cover the inflation gap between 1994 and 1996.
Employers say the claim is excessive and have offered a total 195,000 lire of which 30,000 is to cover inflation.
Michele Figurati, director-general of the employers federation Federmeccanica, said after seeing Treu the meeting had been a step forward after talks had been stalled since last month.

"We did not make any numerical counterproposal but we stated our willingness to remain within the July accord and take all the steps envisaged by the agreement to reach a solution," Figurati told reporters.
UILM union leader Luigi Angeletti told reporters unions and employers would meet Treu separately on Tuesday after talks at a technical level on Friday and Monday.
"Based on the technical meetings, we will evaluate whether conditions exist to start negotiations," Angeletti said.

FIOM leader Claudio Sabattini said: "As things stand now, we dont envisage a solution, but there is a better climate and a willingness by Federmeccanica to restart discussions. We'll judge this next week." ($1=1534 Lire)
